description:
## Goal

Extend `notify_observers/1` to detect when a subscriber's message queue is saturated
and drop the update rather than exacerbating the backlog. Signal the subscriber to
re-subscribe on its next render so it gets a fresh projected value.

Prerequisite: D4 merged.

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance.
Do not improvise.

---

## Design

When `notify_observers/1` iterates subscribers:
1. Check the subscriber's message queue depth via `Process.info/2`
2. If depth ≥ `@max_mailbox_depth`, the process is overloaded
3. Drop the update (do not send `{:filament_observable_update, ...}`)
4. Send `{:filament_observable_resubscribe, fiber_id, slot_index}` to the subscriber instead
5. Log a warning

The LiveView `handle_info` for `:filament_observable_resubscribe` marks the hook slot as
`:needs_resubscribe`. On the next render, `use_observable` (D4) sees `:needs_resubscribe`
and re-subscribes, getting a fresh `initial_value` from the observable.

Because we did not send an update, `subscriber.last_projected` is NOT updated. This
means the next actual notification (after the subscriber catches up) will always fire,
which is correct.

Edge case: `Process.info(pid, :message_queue_len)` returns `nil` if the process is dead.
Treat nil as saturated — the `:DOWN` handler in D2 will clean up the subscriber.

---

## 1. Configuration

FILE: config/config.exs (or application config)

```elixir
config :filament, :observable_max_mailbox_depth, 100
```

This value is read at compile time via `Application.compile_env/3` so it can be zero-cost
at runtime. In tests, override per-test via `Application.put_env/3` with a low threshold
(e.g., 5) to make saturation easy to trigger.

---

## 2. Update notify_observers/1 in Filament.Observable.GenServer

FILE: lib/filament/observable/gen_server.ex

Add a module attribute for the threshold:

```elixir
@max_mailbox_depth Application.compile_env(:filament, :observable_max_mailbox_depth, 100)
```

Update `notify_observers/1` (which already handles change-or-bust from D3). The
saturation check runs BEFORE the change-or-bust check, because a saturated process
needs the resubscribe signal regardless of whether the projected value changed:

```elixir
def notify_observers(new_state) do
  subs = Process.get(:__filament_subscribers__, %{})

  new_subs =
    Map.new(subs, fn {pid, subscriber} ->
      depth =
        case Process.info(subscriber.pid, :message_queue_len) do
          {:message_queue_len, n} -> n
          nil -> :saturated
        end

      if depth == :saturated or depth >= @max_mailbox_depth do
        require Logger
        Logger.warning(
          "[Filament.Observable] subscriber #{inspect(subscriber.pid)} saturated " <>
            "(depth=#{inspect(depth)}), dropping update for fiber #{inspect(subscriber.fiber_id)}"
        )
        send(
          subscriber.pid,
          {:filament_observable_resubscribe, subscriber.fiber_id, subscriber.slot_index}
        )
        # Do NOT update last_projected — next real notification must fire
        {pid, subscriber}
      else
        new_projected = subscriber.project.(new_state)

        if new_projected !== subscriber.last_projected do
          send(
            subscriber.pid,
            {:filament_observable_update, subscriber.fiber_id, subscriber.slot_index, new_projected}
          )
          {pid, %{subscriber | last_projected: new_projected}}
        else
          {pid, subscriber}
        end
      end
    end)

  Process.put(:__filament_subscribers__, new_subs)
  :ok
end
```

---

## 3. LiveView handle_info — resubscribe signal

FILE: lib/filament/live_view.ex
(add alongside the `handle_info({:filament_observable_update, ...})` clause from D4)

```elixir
@impl Phoenix.LiveView
def handle_info({:filament_observable_resubscribe, fiber_id, slot_index}, socket) do
  tree = socket.assigns.filament_tree

  tree =
    Filament.FiberTree.update_hook_slot(tree, fiber_id, slot_index, fn
      {:subscribed, _server, _value} -> :needs_resubscribe
      other -> other
    end)

  {:noreply, Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :filament_tree, tree)}
end
```

Assigning `:filament_tree` triggers a re-render. On the next `use_observable/3` call,
`hook_slots[slot_index] == :needs_resubscribe`, so D4's `do_subscribe/5` re-subscribes
and returns a fresh projected value.

---

## 4. Tests

FILE: test/filament/observable/backpressure_test.exs

Helper to flood a process mailbox:

```elixir
defp flood_mailbox(pid, count) do
  for _ <- 1..count, do: send(pid, :__filler__)
end

defp drain_mailbox do
  receive do
    :__filler__ -> drain_mailbox()
  after
    0 -> :ok
  end
end
```

Set threshold low in tests: `Application.put_env(:filament, :observable_max_mailbox_depth, 5)`
NOTE: because `@max_mailbox_depth` is a compile-time attribute, you cannot override it
at runtime in tests. Instead, test with the DEFAULT threshold of 100 by flooding exactly
100 messages, or — preferably — refactor `notify_observers/1` to accept the threshold as
a parameter with a default of `@max_mailbox_depth`, making it testable without recompilation.
The latter approach is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. Document the decision in a comment.

IMPORTANT: If the compile-time attribute approach makes the backpressure logic untestable
without recompilation, that IS a deviation from this spec. Stop, comment, await guidance.

Test cases:
1. **normal delivery** — subscriber with empty mailbox receives `{:filament_observable_update, ...}`, no resubscribe signal
2. **saturated triggers resubscribe** — flood subscriber mailbox to >= threshold, call `notify_observers/1`, assert subscriber received `{:filament_observable_resubscribe, fiber_id, slot_index}` and did NOT receive `{:filament_observable_update, ...}`
3. **last_projected not updated on saturation** — flood, call `notify_observers(state_a)`, drain, call `notify_observers(state_a)` again: assert second call DOES send an update (because last_projected was never updated to state_a's projection during saturation)
4. **dead process handled gracefully** — subscribe, kill subscriber process (do NOT wait for DOWN to propagate), call `notify_observers/1`, assert no crash
5. **warning logged on saturation** — use ExUnit's `capture_log/1` or `assert_receive` on Logger output, verify warning contains the fiber_id

Run: `mix test test/filament/observable/backpressure_test.exs`

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `notify_observers/1` checks mailbox depth before change-or-bust check
- [ ] Saturated subscriber receives `{:filament_observable_resubscribe, ...}`, not `{:filament_observable_update, ...}`
- [ ] `last_projected` is NOT updated when dropping due to saturation
- [ ] Dead process (nil from `Process.info`) handled without crash
- [ ] LiveView `handle_info({:filament_observable_resubscribe, ...})` sets hook slot to `:needs_resubscribe`
- [ ] All 5 tests pass
- [ ] Dialyzer clean
- [ ] D2–D4 test suites still pass (no regressions)
title: D5: Backpressure — detect saturated subscriber mailbox, drop and signal resubscribe
